pinterest.title: Wedding RSVP Website Guide: Choose the Right Kind for Your Destination Wedding
pinterest.description: A wedding RSVP website is where guests from around the world tell you whether they are coming, which nights they will be there, what they eat and when their flight lands. Compare the main kinds: an all-in-one wedding website, a standalone RSVP tool, an invitation platform, a planning app, or a DIY form plus spreadsheet. Choose by what your weekend needs, such as separate replies for each event and travel questions, rather than by the look of the template.

pinterest.title: Wedding RSVP Website for Several Events: Welcome Dinner, Ceremony and Brunch
pinterest.description: A destination wedding can span a welcome dinner, the ceremony and reception, and a slow brunch the morning after. Look for an online wedding RSVP where one reply covers every event, with a separate yes or no for each. Set invitations by household, ask for meal and dietary needs for each person, add arrival and departure dates, and write your reply date with a date and a time zone so nobody misses it by a day.

pinterest.title: QR Code on Your Wedding Invitation? Print the RSVP Website Address Too
pinterest.description: A QR code on a printed invitation or details card lets guests reach your wedding RSVP website with a phone camera. It is a handy shortcut, with one caution: print the RSVP web address beside the code, short and easy to type, for guests who would rather not scan. Create the code with a trusted, secure tool, then test-scan the printed proof on more than one phone before the full print run.

instagram_carousel.caption:
For a destination wedding, your RSVP website is where your aunt in Perth, your school friends in London and your colleague in Singapore all tell you the same things: whether they are coming, which nights they will be there, what they eat and when their flight lands.

Our refreshed guide compares the kinds of wedding RSVP website without naming platforms, so you can judge any tool on what your weekend asks of it:
- The kinds: an all-in-one wedding website, a standalone RSVP tool, an invitation platform with RSVP built in, a planning app with RSVP, and a DIY form plus spreadsheet.
- What to check before you pay: guest and event limits, custom questions, the tool's branding, a custom domain, password protection, reminder sends, data export and ads shown to guests.
- Destination details: separate RSVPs for each event, travel and accommodation questions, households and plus-ones, meal and dietary needs for each person, and a reply date with a time zone.
- Privacy: ask only for the details your planning needs, password-protect the site, share the list only with the suppliers who need it, and delete what you no longer need after the wedding.
- QR codes: print the RSVP web address beside the code and test-scan the printed proof before the full print run.

Wonderland Studio, our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, keeps your replies and your seating chart in the same place.
